title: Quarterly Business Review Template With 8 Examples and Agenda
summary: Free Quarterly Business Review template, a filled HR example, and a 60-minute meeting agenda. Download the QBR template or copy-paste into any doc tool.
body_markdown:
### What is a quarterly business review (QBR)?


A quarterly business review is a structured meeting held every 90 days where teams evaluate performance against goals, surface risks, and align priorities for the next quarter. Internal QBRs involve department heads presenting KPIs, OKR progress, and resource needs to leadership. External QBRs happen between a vendor and customer to assess value delivered. The core purpose: replace assumptions with data, make decisions with the right people in the room, and leave with clear owners for the next 90 days.


### What should a QBR template include?


Eight sections: KPI scorecard with quarter-over-quarter deltas, OKR or goal progress with status indicators, wins and achievements summary, challenges with root causes and impact, risks flagged with owners and mitigation plans, prior-quarter commitment status, next-quarter priorities with owners and metrics, and decisions required from leadership. The template should be short enough to present in under 30 minutes. Anything longer signals too much narrative and not enough structure.


### How long should a quarterly business review be?


45 to 60 minutes. Roughly 5 minutes for opening context, 15 minutes for KPI and goal review, 10 minutes for challenges and risks, 10 minutes for next-quarter priorities, 10 minutes for discussion and decisions, and 5 minutes to confirm action items. If your QBR regularly exceeds 60 minutes, the deck likely has too many slides or the discussion is drifting into operational detail that belongs in weekly stand-ups.


### How do you prepare for a QBR?


Start two weeks before the meeting. In week one, collect data: pull KPI actuals, update OKR progress, and gather input from team leads on wins, blockers, and resource needs. In week two, build the deck and circulate a pre-read to attendees 48 hours before the meeting. The pre-read should include the KPI scorecard and any decisions you need from leadership, so attendees arrive with context. On meeting day, spend zero time presenting data the room already has. Focus the live session on discussion, trade-offs, and decisions.


### What are the most common QBR mistakes?


The biggest mistakes in quarterly business reviews: presenting raw data without context or recommendations, skipping the review of last quarter’s action items, packing too many slides into the deck, letting the meeting run without time-boxed sections, and not sending a written summary within 24 hours. Another common one is treating the QBR as a status update instead of a decision-making meeting. If no decisions are made and no action items are assigned, the QBR added no value. Keep the deck under 10 slides, start with the metrics that missed target, and end with clear owners for next quarter.


### What KPIs should be in a QBR?


Cap the KPI dashboard at 5-8 metrics that define the business unit or function. For revenue teams: new ARR, net revenue retention, gross churn, CAC payback, pipeline coverage. For product: activation rate, engagement, quarterly release velocity, quality signal. For people teams: hiring plan attainment, regrettable attrition, engagement. Each row needs target, actual, delta, trend and a named decision. A KPI without a decision is just a number on a slide.


### What does a good QBR look like? (Example)


A mid-size HR team’s Q2 QBR opens with four KPIs: time-to-fill dropped from 38 to 29 days, offer acceptance rate held at 88%, regrettable attrition rose from 6% to 9%, and eNPS stayed flat at 42. The OKR section shows two objectives on track (hiring pipeline automation, manager training rollout) and one behind (internal mobility program, blocked by budget approval). Challenges: attrition spike traced to two engineering teams with no stay interviews conducted. The department head proposes three Q3 priorities: launch stay interviews for high-risk teams, backfill three open roles by August, and pilot a promotion calibration process. Leadership approves the backfills, defers the calibration pilot to Q4, and assigns the CHRO to resolve the mobility program budget by end of month. The meeting runs 52 minutes, and the summary email goes out the same afternoon with six action items, each with an owner and a deadline.


### Who should attend a QBR?


Keep the invite tight. Four roles cover most QBRs: the QBR owner (agenda, template, pre-read), function leads (their block), the executive sponsor (cross-function tradeoffs and escalations), and a scribe (real-time action register). A QBR with more than 10 people usually stops making decisions and becomes a broadcast. If a stakeholder needs the outcome but not the discussion, send them the follow-up instead of adding them to the invite.
